content.topic: What is worth doing is worth doing well

modelEssay.title: What is Worth Doing is Worth Doing Well
modelEssay.content:
The adage 'What is worth doing is worth doing well' resonates with many as it encapsulates the essence of commitment and excellence. This principle underscores the idea that if an endeavor is valuable, it deserves our utmost effort and attention.

In various aspects of life, from education to career, this saying holds true. For instance, in academics, students who approach their studies with diligence and dedication often achieve higher grades and deeper understanding. Similarly, professionals who strive for perfection in their work are more likely to excel and advance in their careers. The pursuit of excellence not only leads to better outcomes but also fosters a sense of accomplishment and satisfaction.

In conclusion, the saying serves as a reminder that quality should never be compromised, regardless of the task at hand. It is a call to action for all of us to approach our endeavors with the seriousness and dedication they deserve, thereby reaping the rewards of our labor.

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话一。

transcript.text: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您是牛津大学的物理学教授。

transcript.text: You're a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您是欧洲核子研究组织的高级顾问。

transcript.text: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您似乎还不知疲倦地环游世界，发表演讲。

transcript.text: And, in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 此外，您还有一个每周的科学电视节目。

transcript.text: Where do you get the energy?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您哪里来的精力？

transcript.text: Oh, well, I just love what I do.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 哦，嗯，我只是热爱我的工作。

transcript.text: I'm extremely fortunate to have this life, doing what I love doing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我非常幸运能过上这样的生活，做我热爱的事情。

transcript.text: Professor, what exactly is your goal?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 教授，您的目标到底是什么？

transcript.text: Why do you do all of this?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您为什么做所有这些？

transcript.text: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on, but these, I think, can be divided into two groups, the education of science and the further understanding of science.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，正如您所说，我确实有各种不同的事情在进行，但我认为这些可以分为两类：科学教育和对科学的进一步理解。

transcript.text: Don't these two things get in the way of each other?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这两件事不会相互妨碍吗？

transcript.text: What I mean is, doesn't giving lectures take time away from the lab?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我的意思是，发表演讲不会占用实验室的时间吗？

transcript.text: Not really, no.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不完全是，不会。

transcript.text: I love teaching, and I don't mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我热爱教学，而且我不介意现在比过去花更多时间在教学上。

transcript.text: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 此外，我想说的是，教授一门学科有助于我更好地理解它。

transcript.text: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我发现，当我必须清楚地解释某事、帮助他人理解它以及回答关于它的问题时，这促进了我自己的知识。

transcript.text: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 无论一个人在所教授领域已有多少专业知识，高水平的教学对任何人来说都是非常有激励性的。

transcript.text: Of any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon, a significant discovery or invention we can expect soon.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 关于您预见在不久的将来会出现的任何科学突破，一个重要的发现或发明我们可以期待很快出现。

transcript.text: The world is always conducting science, and there are constantly new things being discovered.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 世界一直在进行科学研究，不断有新事物被发现。

transcript.text: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 事实上，现在我们有太多数据存放在计算机中。

transcript.text: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 例如，我们有数千张由望远镜拍摄的火星照片，但从未有人看过。

transcript.text: We have them, but nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们拥有这些照片，但没有人有时间亲眼查看它们，更不用说分析了。

transcript.text: Conversation two
transcript.translation: 对话二

transcript.text: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你认为梦有特殊含义吗？

transcript.text: No, I don't think they do.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不，我认为没有。

transcript.text: I don't either, but some people do.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我也不认为，但有些人这么认为。

transcript.text: I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我认为那些相信梦有特殊含义的人是迷信的，尤其是在当今。

transcript.text: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在过去，古埃及、古希腊或古中国时期，人们常常相信梦能预见未来。

transcript.text: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但今天，随着我们拥有的所有科学知识，我认为很难再相信这类事情了。

transcript.text: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我的祖母是迷信的，她认为梦能预测未来。

transcript.text: Once, she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有一次，她梦到她第二天要乘坐的航班坠毁了。

transcript.text: Can you guess what she did?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你能猜到她做了什么吗？

transcript.text: She didn't take that flight.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 她没有乘坐那个航班。

transcript.text: She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 她甚至第二天都没有去机场。

transcript.text: Instead, she took the same flight, but a week later.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 相反，她乘坐了同一个航班，但是一周后。

transcript.text: And everything was fine, of course.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当然，一切都没事。

transcript.text: No plane ever crashed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没有任何飞机坠毁。

transcript.text: How funny.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 真有趣。

transcript.text: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你知道吗，飞行实际上比其他任何交通方式都安全？

transcript.text: It's been statistically proven.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这已被统计证明。

transcript.text: People can be so irrational sometimes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们有时会如此非理性。

transcript.text: Yes, absolutely.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，绝对是。

transcript.text: But even if we think they're ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但即使我们认为它们荒谬，情感可能和理性思维一样强大。

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 正是如此。

transcript.text: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们会因为他们的非理性感受而做出各种疯狂的事情。

transcript.text: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但事实上，一些心理学家认为，我们的梦是当天情感和记忆的结果。

transcript.text: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wish would happen.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我想是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说过，儿童的梦通常是他们愿望的简单表现，即他们希望发生的事情。

transcript.text: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但在成年人中，梦是他们更复杂情感的反映。

transcript.text: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand, using the scientific method, something as bizarre as dreams?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 心理学家试图用科学方法理解像梦这样奇异的东西，这难道不有趣吗？

transcript.text: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 心理学就像是对非理性感受的理性研究。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack.
transcript.translation: 当一些科学家探索南极洲表面时，另一些科学家正在深入了解冰层下四公里处的一个巨大水体。

transcript.text: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
transcript.translation: 科学家们在20世纪70年代首次通过使用穿透冰层的无线电波发现了沃斯托克湖。

transcript.text: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
transcript.translation: 自那以后，他们使用声波甚至卫星来绘制这个巨大水体的地图。

transcript.text: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
transcript.translation: 沃斯托克湖的水是如何在冰盖下保持液态的？

transcript.text: The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing, says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
transcript.translation: 威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说，上方厚实的冰川像隔热毯一样，防止水结冰。

transcript.text: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake.
transcript.translation: 此外，来自地球深处的地热可能温暖了这个隐藏的湖泊。

transcript.text: The scientists suspect that microorganisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than two million years.
transcript.translation: 科学家们怀疑，可能有微生物生活在沃斯托克湖中，这些微生物已与外界隔绝超过两百万年。

transcript.text: Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth, says Siegert.
transcript.translation: 西格特说，在那里发现的任何东西都将与地球表面的东西完全不同。

transcript.text: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
transcript.translation: 科学家们正在努力找到一种方法，钻入冰层并提取水样，而不造成污染。

transcript.text: Again, robots might be the solution.
transcript.translation: 同样，机器人可能是解决方案。

transcript.text: If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will melt through the surface ice.
transcript.translation: 如果一切按计划进行，一个钻头形状的机器人将融化穿透表面冰层。

transcript.text: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
transcript.translation: 当它到达湖泊时，它将释放另一个机器人，该机器人可以在湖中游泳、拍照并寻找生命迹象。

transcript.text: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and arid conditions.
transcript.translation: 科学家们希望他们的发现能揭示外太空生命，这些生命可能存在于类似的黑暗和干旱条件中。

transcript.text: Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter's moon Europa showed signs of water beneath its icy surface.
transcript.translation: 最近，木星卫星欧罗巴的近距离图片显示了其冰层下有水的迹象。

transcript.text: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there, too.
transcript.translation: 一旦在南极洲测试过，机器人也可以被派往欧罗巴去寻找那里的生命。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984 when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
transcript.translation: 1984年，詹姆斯·科普兰产生了研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人的想法，当时他发现关于他们的语言研究很少。

transcript.text: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
transcript.translation: 他通过一位在墨西哥与部落成员合作的社会工作者联系到了一位部落成员。

transcript.text: At first, the tribe member, named Gonzales, was very reluctant to cooperate.
transcript.translation: 起初，这位名叫冈萨雷斯的部落成员非常不愿意合作。

transcript.text: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language.
transcript.translation: 他告诉科普兰，再多的钱也买不到他的语言。

transcript.text: But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research, and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzales agreed to help.
transcript.translation: 但在科普兰向他解释了他的研究意图，以及这将如何使塔拉乌马拉人受益后，冈萨雷斯同意帮忙。

transcript.text: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
transcript.translation: 他带科普兰去了他的村庄，并担任了中间人。

transcript.text: Copeland says, thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us.
transcript.translation: 科普兰说，多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人明白了我们的使命，并开始信任我们。

transcript.text: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
transcript.translation: 进入塔拉乌马拉人的世界对科普兰来说是一个艰巨的项目。

transcript.text: To reach their homeland, he must drive two and a half days from Houston, Texas.
transcript.translation: 要到达他们的家园，他必须从得克萨斯州休斯顿开车两天半。

transcript.text: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get, and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
transcript.translation: 他装满车辆，带上部落成员不易获得的物品，并将这些物品作为友谊的象征送给他们。

transcript.text: The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
transcript.translation: 塔拉乌马拉人不相信积累财富，他们接收食物并互相分享。

transcript.text: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, it also has enriched his life in several ways.
transcript.translation: 对科普兰来说，这次经历不仅在学术上令人满意，还在多个方面丰富了他的生活。

transcript.text: I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the tradition, he says.
transcript.translation: 他说：“我看到人们拒绝技术，过着非常艰苦的传统生活，这让我对传统中进步的意义有了另一种理解。”

transcript.text: I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
transcript.translation: 我体验了在自然中生活的简单，否则我只能从书本上读到。

transcript.text: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other.
transcript.translation: 我在他们的分享意识和相互关怀中看到了很多美好。

transcript.text: Followed by three or four questions.
transcript.translation: 随后是三个或四个问题。

transcript.text: What is a radical?
transcript.translation: 什么是激进分子？

transcript.text: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them.
transcript.translation: 如今人们似乎对这个词感到恐惧，尤其是害怕被贴上这个标签。

transcript.text: Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white male in Western society.
transcript.translation: 指控个人或团体激进通常是为了迫使他们沉默屈服，从而维持现状，更重要的是，保护西方社会中少数富裕白人男性的权力。

transcript.text: Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
transcript.translation: 女权主义是这一现象的绝佳例证。

transcript.text: The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism, when the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
transcript.translation: 妇女运动一直受到刻板印象、媒体的错误描绘以及仇视男性和激进主义的指控所困扰，而女权主义的基本基础仅仅是女性在生活的所有方面应享有平等权利。

transcript.text: When faced with the threat of being labeled radical, women back down from their worthy cause and consequently participate in their own oppression.
transcript.translation: 当面临被贴上激进标签的威胁时，女性从她们有价值的事业中退缩，从而参与了对自身的压迫。

transcript.text: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word.
transcript.translation: 已经到了这样一个地步，许多女性因为这个词所带的污名而不敢自称女权主义者。

transcript.text: If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
transcript.translation: 如果人们拒绝被污名所控制和恐吓，污名就会失去所有力量。

transcript.text: Without fear on which to feed, such stigmas can only die.
transcript.translation: 没有恐惧可以滋养，这样的污名只能消亡。

transcript.text: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
transcript.translation: 在我看来，激进分子就是反抗规范或倡导改变现状的人。

transcript.text: On closer inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
transcript.translation: 仔细观察就会发现，规范是不断演变的，因此不是固定不变的实体。

transcript.text: So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation?
transcript.translation: 那么，为什么偏离现状如此具有威胁性，而现状本身却不稳定且不断变化呢？

transcript.text: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the rise of those who don't.
transcript.translation: 这一切都归结于维护掌权者的权力并防止无权者崛起。

transcript.text: In fact, when we look at the word radical in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
transcript.translation: 事实上，当我们从历史背景来看“激进”这个词时，我们现在推崇为英雄的几乎每一个人在他或她的时代都被视为激进分子。

transcript.text: Radicals are people who affect change.
transcript.translation: 激进分子是影响变革的人。

transcript.text: They are the people about whom history is written.
transcript.translation: 他们是历史记载的人物。

transcript.text: Abolitionists were radicals.
transcript.translation: 废奴主义者是激进分子。

transcript.text: Civil rights activists were radicals.
transcript.translation: 民权活动家是激进分子。

transcript.text: Even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
transcript.translation: 甚至我们国家的创始人为赢得从英国的独立而战时也是激进分子。

transcript.text: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
transcript.translation: 他们在历史上的存在改变了我们社会的运作方式，主要是通过改变先前存在的权力平衡。

transcript.text: Of course, there are some radicals who've made a negative impact on humanity, but undeniably there would simply be no progress without radicals.
transcript.translation: 当然，有些激进分子对人类产生了负面影响，但不可否认的是，没有激进分子就根本没有进步。

transcript.text: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
transcript.translation: 话虽如此，下次有人称我为激进分子时，我将自豪地接受这个标签。

transcript.text: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
transcript.translation: 我们非常容易受到周围人的影响。

transcript.text: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so and has returned with an accent perhaps.
transcript.translation: 例如，你可能认识某人，他出国一年左右，回来后可能带点口音。

transcript.text: We become part of our immediate environment.
transcript.translation: 我们成为我们直接环境的一部分。

transcript.text: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world and let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
transcript.translation: 我们中没有人能免疫自己世界的影响，别自欺欺人地认为我们不受生活中事物和人的影响。

transcript.text: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory.
transcript.translation: Fred去工厂开始他的新工作。

transcript.text: Fred takes a 10-minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
transcript.translation: Fred休息10分钟喝咖啡，但其他工人休息半小时。

transcript.text: Fred says, what's the matter with you guys?
transcript.translation: Fred说，你们怎么了？

transcript.text: Weeks later, Fred is taking 20-minute breaks.
transcript.translation: 几周后，Fred休息20分钟。

transcript.text: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
transcript.translation: 一个月后，Fred也休息半小时。

transcript.text: Fred is saying, if you can't beat them, join them.
transcript.translation: Fred说，如果打不过他们，就加入他们。

transcript.text: Why would I work any harder than the next guy?
transcript.translation: 我为什么要比别人更努力工作？

transcript.text: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
transcript.translation: 关于为人最有趣的是，通常我们没有意识到心态正在发生变化。

transcript.text: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air.
transcript.translation: 这就像在新鲜空气里待了几周后回到城市烟雾中一样。

transcript.text: Only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells.
transcript.translation: 直到那时我们才意识到自己已经习惯了那些难闻的气味。

transcript.text: Mix with critical people and we learn to criticize.
transcript.translation: 与挑剔的人交往，我们就学会批评。

transcript.text: Mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
transcript.translation: 与快乐的人交往，我们就学会快乐。

transcript.text: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
transcript.translation: 这意味着我们需要决定从生活中想要什么，然后相应地选择我们的同伴。

transcript.text: You may well say, that is going to take some effort.
transcript.translation: 你可能会说，这需要一些努力。

transcript.text: It may not be comfortable.
transcript.translation: 可能不会很舒适。

transcript.text: I may offend some of my present company.
transcript.translation: 我可能会冒犯我现在的一些同伴。

transcript.text: Right, but it is your life.
transcript.translation: 没错，但这是你的生活。

transcript.text: Fred may say, I'm always broke, frequently depressed, I'm going nowhere, and I never do anything exciting.
transcript.translation: Fred可能会说，我总是破产，经常沮丧，一事无成，从不做任何令人兴奋的事。

transcript.text: Then we discover that Fred's best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere, and wishing that life was more exciting.
transcript.translation: 然后我们发现Fred的最好朋友也总是破产，经常沮丧，一事无成，并希望生活更刺激。

transcript.text: This is not coincidence, nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
transcript.translation: 这不是巧合，我们也无权评判Fred。

transcript.text: However, if Fred wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he'll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years.
transcript.translation: 然而，如果Fred想改善生活质量，他首先需要认识到这些年到底发生了什么。

transcript.text: It's no surprise that doctors, as a profession, suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
transcript.translation: 医生这个职业身体健康问题多不足为奇，因为他们一生都与病人打交道。

transcript.text: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
transcript.translation: 由于相关原因，精神科医生职业中的自杀率较高。

transcript.text: Traditionally, nine out of ten children whose parents smoke, smoke themselves.
transcript.translation: 传统上，父母吸烟的孩子中，十个有九个自己也吸烟。

transcript.text: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
transcript.translation: 肥胖部分是一个环境问题。

transcript.text: Successful people are successful friends and so the story goes on.
transcript.translation: 成功的人有成功的朋友，如此循环往复。

transcript.text: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
transcript.translation: 几乎每个美国人只需一眼就能认出美元钞票。

transcript.text: Many can identify it by its sound or texture, but few people indeed can accurately describe the world's most powerful important currency.
transcript.translation: 许多人能通过声音或质地识别它，但确实很少有人能准确描述世界上最强大、最重要的货币。

transcript.text: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other.
transcript.translation: 美国美元钞票一面用黑色墨水印刷，另一面用绿色墨水印刷。

transcript.text: The exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
transcript.translation: 纸张和墨水的确切成分是政府严密保守的秘密。

transcript.text: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
transcript.translation: 尽管它非常重要，但美元钞票实际上很轻。

transcript.text: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
transcript.translation: 需要近500张钞票才能使天平达到一磅的重量。

transcript.text: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief lifespan.
transcript.translation: 美元钞票不仅轻便，而且寿命短暂。

transcript.text: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
transcript.translation: 很少有美元钞票能存活超过18个月。

transcript.text: The word dollar is taken from the German word Tala, the name for the world's most important currency in the 16th century.
transcript.translation: 美元一词源自德语单词Tala，这是16世纪世界上最重要货币的名称。

transcript.text: The Tala was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany.
transcript.translation: Tala是一种银币，于1518年在德国皇帝查理五世统治时期首次铸造。

transcript.text: The concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
transcript.translation: 纸币的概念在美国货币史上是一个相对较新的创新。

transcript.text: When the constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
transcript.translation: 当宪法签署时，由于纸币在殖民时代价值持续下降，人们对纸币评价不高。

transcript.text: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted many coins for common currency.
transcript.translation: 由于这种缺乏信任，新美国政府铸造了许多硬币作为通用货币。

transcript.text: Interest-bearing banknotes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
transcript.translation: 同时发行了带利息的钞票，但其目的仅限于为紧急政府危机提供资金，例如美国参与1812年战争。

transcript.text: The first non-interest-bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862 at the height of the Civil War.
transcript.translation: 第一张无息纸币于1862年美国内战最激烈时由国会授权发行。

transcript.text: At this point, citizens' old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
transcript.translation: 此时，公民对贬值纸币的旧有恐惧已经平息，美元钞票由此诞生。

transcript.text: The new green-colored paper money quickly earned the name greenback.
transcript.translation: 新的绿色纸币很快获得了“绿背钞票”的名称。

transcript.text: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve and is issued from the twelve Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
transcript.translation: 如今，美国美元钞票是美联储的产物，由美国各地的十二家联邦储备银行发行。

transcript.text: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately two billion bills in circulation at all times.
transcript.translation: 政府始终维持约二十亿张钞票的稳定流通供应。

paragraphs.text: Overall, men are more likely than women to make excuses. Several studies suggest that men feel the need to appear competent in all __26__, while women worry only about the skills in which they've invested __27__. Ask a man and a woman to go diving for the first time, and the woman is likely to jump in, while the man is likely to say he's not feeling too well.
paragraphs.translation: 总体上，男性比女性更可能找借口。多项研究表明，男性觉得需要在所有领域显得有竞争力，而女性只担心她们投入大量精力的技能。如果让一个男人和一个女人第一次去潜水，女人可能会跳进去，而男人可能会说他不太舒服。

paragraphs.text: Ironically, it is often success that leads people to flirt with failure. Praise won for __28__ a skill suddenly puts one in the position of having everything to lose. Rather than putting their reputation on the line again, many successful people develop a handicap-drinking, __29__, depression--that allows them to keep their status no matter what the future brings. An advertising executive __30__ for depression shortly after winning an award put it this way: "Without my depression, I'd be a failure now; with it, I'm a success 'on hold.'"
paragraphs.translation: 讽刺的是，往往是成功引导人们与失败调情。掌握一项技能所获得的赞扬突然使人处于可能失去一切的境地。许多成功人士为了不冒险损害自己的声誉，会发展出一种障碍——饮酒、疲劳、抑郁——以便无论未来如何都能保持自己的地位。一位在获奖后不久因抑郁症住院的广告高管这样说：‘没有我的抑郁症，我现在就是个失败者；有了它，我就是个暂停的成功者。’

paragraphs.text: In fact, the people most likely to become chronic excuse makers are those __31__ with success. Such people are so afraid of being __32__ a failure at anything that they constantly develop one handicap or another in order to explain away failure.
paragraphs.translation: 事实上，最可能成为长期找借口者的是那些沉迷于成功的人。这些人非常害怕在任何事情上被贴上失败的标签，以至于他们不断制造这样或那样的障碍来解释失败。

paragraphs.text: Though self-handicapping can be an effective way of coping with performance anxiety now and then, in the end, researchers say, it will lead to __33__. In the long run, excuse makers fail to live up to their true __34__ and lose the status they care so much about. And despite their protests to the __35__, they have only themselves to blame.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管自我设障碍偶尔可能是应对表现焦虑的有效方式，但研究人员表示，最终它会导致毁灭。从长远来看，找借口者无法发挥他们真正的潜力，并失去他们非常在乎的地位。尽管他们对相互性提出抗议，但他们只能怪自己。

questionGroups.title: Six Potential Brain Benefits of Bilingual Education

material.title: Six Potential Brain Benefits of Bilingual Education

paragraphs.text: Brains, brains, brains. People are fascinated by brain research. And yet it can be hard to point to places where our education system is really making use of the latest neuroscience (神经科学) findings. But there is one happy link where research is meeting practice: bilingual (双语的) education. "In the last 20 years or so, there's been a virtual explosion of research on bilingualism," says Judith Kroll, a professor at the University of California, Riverside.
paragraphs.translation: 大脑，大脑，大脑。人们对大脑研究很着迷。然而，很难指出我们的教育系统在哪些地方真正利用了最新的神经科学发现。但有一个令人欣喜的联系，那就是研究正在与实践结合：双语教育。“在过去20年左右的时间里，关于双语的研究几乎出现了爆炸性增长，”加州大学河滨分校的教授Judith Kroll说。

paragraphs.text: Again and again, researchers have found, "bilingualism is an experience that shapes our brain for life," in the words of Gigi Luk, an associate professor at Harvard's Graduate School of Education. At the same time, one of the hottest trends in public schooling is what's often called dual-language or two-way immersion programs.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人员一再发现，“双语是一种塑造我们大脑终生的经历，”用哈佛大学教育研究生院的副教授Gigi Luk的话来说。与此同时，公立学校中最热门的趋势之一是通常所说的双语或双向沉浸式项目。

paragraphs.text: Traditional programs for English-language learners, or ELLs, focus on assimilating students into English as quickly as possible. Dual-language classrooms, by contrast, provide instruction across subjects to both English natives and English learners, in both English and a target language. The goal is functional bilingualism and biliteracy for all students by middle school. New York City, North Carolina, Delaware, Utah, Oregon and Washington state are among the places expanding dual language classrooms.
paragraphs.translation: 针对英语学习者（或ELLs）的传统项目侧重于让学生尽快融入英语。相比之下，双语课堂为英语母语者和英语学习者提供跨学科的教学，使用英语和一种目标语言。目标是到中学时所有学生都能实现功能性双语和双文能力。纽约市、北卡罗来纳州、特拉华州、犹他州、俄勒冈州和华盛顿州等地正在扩大双语课堂。

paragraphs.text: The trend flies in the face of some of the culture wars of two decades ago, when advocates insisted on "English first" education. Most famously, California passed Proposition 227 in 1998. It was intended to sharply reduce the amount of time that English-language learners spent in bilingual settings. Proposition 58, passed by California voters on November 8, largely reversed that decision, paving the way for a huge expansion of bilingual education in the state that has the largest population of English-language learners.
paragraphs.translation: 这一趋势与二十年前的一些文化战争背道而驰，当时倡导者坚持“英语优先”教育。最著名的是，加利福尼亚州在1998年通过了227号提案。该提案旨在大幅减少英语学习者在双语环境中花费的时间。11月8日加利福尼亚州选民通过的58号提案在很大程度上推翻了这一决定，为该州拥有最大英语学习者人口的双语教育的巨大扩张铺平了道路。

paragraphs.text: Some of the insistence on English-first was founded on research produced decades ago, in which bilingual students underperformed monolingual (单语的) English speakers and had lower IQ scores. Today's scholars, like Ellen Bialystok at York University in Toronto, say that research was "deeply flawed." "Earlier research looked at socially disadvantaged groups," agrees Antonella Sorace at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. "This has been completely contradicted by recent research" that compares groups more similar to each other.
paragraphs.translation: 一些坚持英语优先的观点基于几十年前的研究，该研究显示双语学生表现不如单语英语使用者，并且智商分数较低。今天的学者，如多伦多约克大学的Ellen Bialystok，说这项研究“存在严重缺陷”。“早期研究关注社会弱势群体，”苏格兰爱丁堡大学的Antonella Sorace同意道。“这已被最近的研究完全反驳”，这些研究比较了更相似的群体。

paragraphs.text: So what does recent research say about the potential benefits of bilingual education? It turns out that, in many ways, the real trick to speaking two languages consists in managing not to speak one of those languages at a given moment — which is fundamentally a feat of paying attention. Saying "Goodbye" to mom and then "Guten tag" to your teacher, or managing to ask for a crayola roja instead of a red crayon (蜡笔), requires skills called "inhibition" and "task switching." These skills are a subset of an ability called executive function.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，最近的研究对双语教育的潜在益处说了什么？事实证明，在许多方面，说两种语言的真正诀窍在于在特定时刻管理不说其中一种语言——这本质上是一种注意力的壮举。对妈妈说“再见”，然后对老师说“Guten tag”，或者设法要一支crayola roja而不是一支红色蜡笔，需要称为“抑制”和“任务切换”的技能。这些技能是称为执行功能的一种能力的子集。

paragraphs.text: People who speak two languages often outperform monolinguals on general measures of executive function. "Bilinguals can pay focused attention without being distracted and also improve in the ability to switch from one task to another," says Sorace.
paragraphs.translation: 会说两种语言的人在执行功能的总体测量上通常优于单语者。“双语者能够集中注意力而不分心，并且也提高了从一个任务切换到另一个任务的能力，”Sorace说。

paragraphs.text: Do these same advantages benefit a child who begins learning a second language in kindergarten instead of as a baby? We don't yet know. Patterns of language learning and language use are complex. But Gigi Luk at Harvard cites at least one brain-imaging study on adolescents that shows similar changes in brain structure when compared with those who are bilingual from birth, even when they didn't begin practicing a second language in earnest before late childhood.
paragraphs.translation: 这些同样的优势是否惠及那些在幼儿园而不是婴儿时期开始学习第二语言的儿童？我们还不知道。语言学习和语言使用的模式很复杂。但哈佛大学的Gigi Luk引用了至少一项对青少年的脑成像研究，该研究显示，与那些从出生起就是双语者相比，大脑结构有类似的变化，即使他们在童年晚期之前没有认真开始练习第二语言。

paragraphs.text: Young children being raised bilingual have to follow social cues to figure out which language to use with which person and in what setting. As a result, says Sorace, bilingual children as young as age 3 have demonstrated a head start on tests of perspective-taking and theory of mind-both of which are fundamental social and emotional skills.
paragraphs.translation: 被抚养为双语的幼儿必须遵循社交线索来确定与哪个人在什么场合使用哪种语言。因此，Sorace说，年仅3岁的双语儿童在观点采择和心智理论测试中表现出领先，这两者都是基本的社交和情感技能。

paragraphs.text: About 10 percent of students in the Portland, Oregon public schools are assigned by lottery to dual language classrooms that offer instruction in Spanish, Japanese or Mandarin, alongside English. Jennifer Steele at American University conducted a four-year, randomized trial and found that these dual-language students outperformed their peers in English-reading skills by a full school-year's worth of learning by the end of middle school. Because the effects are found in reading, not in math or science where there were few differences, Steele suggests that learning two languages makes students more aware of how language works in general.
paragraphs.translation: 在俄勒冈州波特兰市的公立学校中，大约10%的学生通过抽签被分配到提供西班牙语、日语或普通话教学以及英语的双语课堂。美利坚大学的Jennifer Steele进行了一项为期四年的随机试验，发现这些双语学生在中学结束时，在英语阅读技能上比同龄人领先整整一个学年的学习量。由于效果出现在阅读方面，而在数学或科学方面差异不大，Steele认为学习两种语言使学生更了解语言的一般运作方式。

paragraphs.text: The research of Gigi Luk at Harvard offers a slightly different explanation. She has recently done a small study looking at a group of 100 fourth-graders in Massachusetts who had similar reading scores on a standard test, but very different language experiences. Some were foreign-language dominant and others were English natives. Here's what's interesting. The students who were dominant in a foreign language weren't yet comfortably bilingual; they were just starting to learn English. Therefore, by definition, they had a much weaker English vocabulary than the native speakers. Yet they were just as good at interpreting a text. "This is very surprising," Luk says. "You would expect the reading comprehension performance to mirror the vocabulary--it's a cornerstone of comprehension."
paragraphs.translation: 哈佛大学Gigi Luk的研究提供了一个略有不同的解释。她最近进行了一项小型研究，观察了马萨诸塞州100名四年级学生，他们在标准测试中的阅读分数相似，但语言经历非常不同。一些是外语主导，另一些是英语母语者。有趣的是，那些以一门外语为主导的学生还不太舒适地使用双语；他们刚开始学习英语。因此，从定义上讲，他们的英语词汇量远弱于母语使用者。然而，他们在解释文本方面同样出色。“这非常令人惊讶，”Luk说。“你可能会期望阅读理解表现与词汇量一致——它是理解的基石。

paragraphs.text: How did the foreign-language dominant speakers manage this feat? Well, Luk found, they also scored higher on tests of executive functioning. So, even though they didn't have huge mental dictionaries to draw on, they may have been great puzzle-solvers, taking into account higher-level concepts such as whether a single sentence made sense within an overall story line. They got the same results as the monolinguals, by a different path.
paragraphs.translation: 外语主导的说话者如何实现这一壮举？嗯，Luk发现，他们在执行功能测试中也得分更高。所以，即使他们没有庞大的心理词典可供利用，他们可能是优秀的解题者，考虑到更高层次的概念，比如一个句子在整个故事情节中是否有意义。他们通过不同的路径得到了与单语者相同的结果。

paragraphs.text: American public school classrooms as a whole are becoming more segregated by race and class. Dual-language programs can be an exception. Because they are composed of native English speakers deliberately placed together with recent immigrants, they tend to be more ethnically and economically balanced. And there is some evidence that this helps kids of all backgrounds gain comfort with diversity and different cultures.
paragraphs.translation: 美国公立学校课堂整体上正变得更加按种族和阶级隔离。双语项目可能是一个例外。因为它们由英语母语者与最近移民有意组合在一起，所以往往在民族和经济上更加平衡。并且有证据表明，这有助于所有背景的孩子对多样性和不同文化感到舒适。

paragraphs.text: Several of the researchers also pointed out that, in bilingual education, non-English-dominant students and their families tend to feel that their home language is heard and valued, compared with a classroom where the home language is left at the door in favor of English. This can improve students' sense of belonging and increase parents' involvement in their children's education, including behaviors like reading to children. "Many parents fear their language is an obstacle, a problem, and if they abandon it their child will integrate better," says Antonella Sorace of the University of Edinburgh. "We tell them they're not doing their child a favor by giving up their language."
paragraphs.translation: 几位研究人员还指出，在双语教育中，非英语主导的学生及其家庭往往感到他们的母语被倾听和重视，相比之下，在课堂上母语被留在门外以英语为主。这可以提高学生的归属感，并增加父母参与孩子教育的程度，包括为孩子阅读等行为。“许多父母担心他们的语言是一种障碍，一个问题，如果他们放弃它，他们的孩子会更好地融入，”爱丁堡大学的Antonella Sorace说。“我们告诉他们，放弃语言并不是在帮孩子忙。

paragraphs.text: One theme that was striking in speaking to all these researchers was just how strongly they advocated for dual-language classrooms. Thomas and Collier have advised many school systems on how to expand their dual-language programs, and Sorace runs "Bilingualism Matters," an international network of researchers who promote bilingual education projects. This type of advocacy among scientists is unusual; even more so because the "bilingual advantage hypothesis" is being challenged once again.
paragraphs.translation: 在与所有这些研究人员交谈时，一个突出的主题是他们如此强烈地倡导双语课堂。Thomas和Collier在许多学校系统就如何扩大双语项目提供建议，Sorace运营着“Bilingualism Matters”，这是一个促进双语教育项目的国际研究人员网络。科学家中的这种倡导是不寻常的；更不寻常的是因为“双语优势假说”再次受到挑战。

paragraphs.text: A review of studies published last year found that cognitive advantages failed to appear in 83 percent of published studies, though in a separate analysis, the sum of effects was still significantly positive. One potential explanation offered by the researchers is that advantages that are measurable in the very young and very old tend to fade when testing young adults at the peak of their cognitive powers. And, they countered that no negative effects of bilingual education have been found. So, even if the advantages are small, they are still worth it. Not to mention one obvious, outstanding fact: "Bilingual children can speak two languages!"
paragraphs.translation: 去年发表的一项研究综述发现，在已发表的研究中，有83%的研究未能显示出认知优势，尽管在一项单独的分析中，效果总和仍然显著为正。研究人员提出的一个潜在解释是，在非常年幼和年老的人群中可测量的优势，在测试认知能力处于巅峰的年轻人时往往会消失。并且，他们反驳说，没有发现双语教育的负面效应。所以，即使优势很小，它们仍然值得。更不用说一个明显、突出的事实：“双语儿童会说两种语言！”

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: It is not controversial to say that an unhealthy diet causes bad health. Nor are the basic elements of healthy eating disputed. Obesity raises susceptibility to cancer, and Britain is the sixth most obese country on Earth. That is a public health emergency. But naming the problem is the easy part. No one disputes the costs in quality of life and depleted health budgets of an obese population, but the quest for solutions gets diverted by ideological arguments around responsibility and choice. And the water is muddied by lobbying from the industries that profit from consumption of obesity-inducing products.
paragraphs.translation: 说不健康的饮食导致健康问题是没有争议的。健康饮食的基本要素也没有争议。肥胖增加患癌风险，英国是世界上第六大肥胖国。这是一个公共卫生紧急状况。但指出问题所在只是容易的部分。没人会否认肥胖人群对生活质量和医疗预算消耗的成本，但寻求解决方案的努力却因围绕责任和选择的意识形态争论而偏离方向。而那些从导致肥胖的产品消费中获利的行业游说更是搅浑了水。

paragraphs.text: Historical precedent suggests that science and politics can overcome resistance from businesses that pollute and poison but it takes time, and success often starts small. So it is heartening to note that a programme in Leeds has achieved a reduction in childhood obesity, becoming the first UK city to reverse a fattening trend. The best results were among younger children and in more deprived areas. When 28% of English children aged two to 15 are obese, a national shift on the scale achieved by Leeds would lengthen hundreds of thousands of lives. A significant factor in the Leeds experience appears to be a scheme called HENRY, which helps parents reward behaviours that prevent obesity in children.
paragraphs.translation: 历史先例表明，科学和政治能够克服污染和毒害企业的抵抗，但这需要时间，而且成功往往从小处开始。因此，令人鼓舞的是，利兹的一个项目实现了儿童肥胖率的下降，成为英国首个扭转肥胖趋势的城市。最佳效果出现在年幼儿童和更贫困的地区。当28%的2至15岁英国儿童肥胖时，全国范围内若达到利兹所实现的规模，将能延长数十万人的生命。利兹经验的一个重要因素似乎是一个名为HENRY的计划，它帮助父母奖励防止儿童肥胖的行为。

paragraphs.text: Many members of parliament are uncomfortable even with their own government's anti-obesity strategy, since it involves a "sugar tax" and a ban on the sale of energy drinks to under-16s. Bans and taxes can be blunt instruments, but their harshest critics can rarely suggest better methods. These critics just oppose regulation itself.
paragraphs.translation: 许多议员甚至对本国政府的反肥胖战略感到不适，因为它涉及“糖税”和禁止向16岁以下青少年销售能量饮料。禁令和税收可能是生硬的工具，但最严厉的批评者很少能提出更好的方法。这些批评者只是反对监管本身。

paragraphs.text: The relationship between poor health and inequality is too pronounced for governments to be passive about large-scale intervention. People living in the most deprived areas are four times more prone to die from avoidable causes than counterparts in more affluent places. As the structural nature of public health problems becomes harder to ignore, the complaint about overprotective government loses potency.
paragraphs.translation: 健康不佳与不平等之间的关系如此明显，以至于政府不能对大规模干预持被动态度。生活在最贫困地区的人死于可避免原因的可能性是富裕地区同类人的四倍。随着公共卫生问题的结构性本质越来越难以忽视，对过度保护政府的抱怨也失去了效力。

paragraphs.text: In fact, the polarised debate over public health interventions should have been abandoned long ago. Government action works when individuals are motivated to respond. Individuals need governments that expand access to good choices. The HENRY programme was delivered in part through children's centres. Closing such centres and cutting council budgets doesn't magically increase reserves of individual self-reliance. The function of a well-designed state intervention is not to deprive people of liberty but to build social capacity and infrastructure that helps people take responsibility for their wellbeing. The obesity crisis will not have a solution devised by left or right ideology--but experience indicates that the private sector needs the incentive of regulation before it starts taking public health emergencies seriously.
paragraphs.translation: 事实上，关于公共卫生干预的极化争论早该被摒弃。政府行动在个人有动力响应时才有效。个人需要政府扩大获得良好选择的机会。HENRY计划部分通过儿童中心实施。关闭此类中心和削减议会预算并不能神奇地增加个人自力更生的能力。精心设计的国家干预的功能不是剥夺人们的自由，而是建设社会能力和基础设施，帮助人们对自己的健康负责。肥胖危机不会有由左翼或右翼意识形态制定的解决方案——但经验表明，私营部门需要监管的激励，才能开始认真对待公共卫生紧急状况。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Home to virgin reefs, rare sharks and vast numbers of exotic fish, the Coral Sea is a unique haven of biodiversity off the northeastern coast of Australia. If a proposal by the Australian government goes ahead, the region will also become the world's largest marine protected area, with restrictions or bans on fishing, mining and marine farming.
paragraphs.translation: 珊瑚海是原始珊瑚礁、稀有鲨鱼和大量珍奇鱼类的家园，是澳大利亚东北海岸外独特的生物多样性避风港。如果澳大利亚政府的提案得以实施，该地区还将成为世界上最大的海洋保护区，对捕鱼、采矿和海洋养殖实施限制或禁令。

paragraphs.text: The Coral Sea reserve would cover almost 990 000 square kilometres and stretch as far as 1 100 kilometres from the coast. Unveiled recently by environment minister Tony Burke, the proposal would be the last in a series of proposed marine reserves around Australia's coast.
paragraphs.translation: 珊瑚海保护区将覆盖近99万平方公里，从海岸延伸至1100公里。环境部长托尼·伯克最近公布的这一提案，将是澳大利亚沿海一系列拟议海洋保护区中的最后一个。

paragraphs.text: But the scheme is attracting criticism from scientists and conservation groups, who argue that the government hasn't gone far enough in protecting the Coral Sea, or in other marine reserves in the coastal network.
paragraphs.translation: 但这一计划正受到科学家和环保组织的批评，他们认为政府在保护珊瑚海或其他沿海网络海洋保护区方面做得还不够。

paragraphs.text: Hugh Possingham, director of the Centre of Excellence for Environmental Decisions at the University of Queensland, points out that little more than half of the Coral Sea reserve is proposed as "no take" area, in which all fishing would be banned. The world's largest existing marine reserve, established last year by the British government in the Indian Ocean, spans 654 000 km2 and is a no-take zone throughout. An alliance of campaigning conversation groups argues that more of the Coral Sea should receive this level of protection.
paragraphs.translation: 昆士兰大学环境决策卓越中心主任休·波辛汉指出，珊瑚海保护区中只有略多于一半的区域被提议为“禁捕区”，所有捕鱼活动将被禁止。英国政府去年在印度洋建立的全球现有最大海洋保护区覆盖65.4万平方公里，全部为禁捕区。一个由环保倡导组织组成的联盟认为，珊瑚海应有更多区域获得这一级别的保护。

paragraphs.text: "I would like to have seen more protection for coral reefs," says Terry Hughes, director of the Centre of Excellence for Coral Reef Studies at James Cook University in Queensland. "More than 20 of them would be outside the no-take area and vulnerable to catch-and-release fishing".
paragraphs.translation: 昆士兰詹姆斯·库克大学珊瑚礁卓越研究中心主任特里·休斯说：“我希望对珊瑚礁有更多的保护。超过20个珊瑚礁将位于禁捕区之外，容易受到捕捞后释放捕鱼活动的影响。”

paragraphs.text: As Nature went to press, the Australian government had not responded to specific criticisms of the plan. But Robin Beaman, a marine geologist at James Cook University, says that the reserve does "broadly protect the range of habitats" in the sea. "I can testify to the huge effort that government agencies and other organisations have put into trying to understand the ecological values of this vast area," he says.
paragraphs.translation: 在《自然》杂志付印时，澳大利亚政府尚未对该计划的具体批评作出回应。但詹姆斯·库克大学海洋地质学家罗宾·比曼表示，该保护区确实“广泛保护了海洋中的栖息地范围”。他说：“我可以证明，政府机构和其他组织为理解这一广阔区域的生态价值付出了巨大努力。”

paragraphs.text: Reserves proposed earlier this year for Australia's southwestern and northwestern coastal regions have also been criticised for failing to give habitats adequate protection. In August, 173 marine scientists signed an open letter to the government saying they were "greatly concerned" that the proposals for the southwestern region had not been based on the "core science principles" of reserves--the protected regions were not, for instance, representative of all the habitats in the region, they said.
paragraphs.translation: 今年早些时候为澳大利亚西南部和西北部沿海地区提出的保护区也因未能为栖息地提供充分保护而受到批评。8月，173名海洋科学家签署了一封致政府的公开信，表示他们“非常担忧”西南部地区的提案没有基于保护区的“核心科学原则”——例如，保护区并不代表该地区的所有栖息地。

paragraphs.text: Critics say that the southwestern reserve offers the greatest protection to the offshore areas where commercial opportunities are fewest and where there is little threat to the environment, a contention also levelled at the Coral Sea plan.
paragraphs.translation: 批评者称，西南部保护区为商业机会最少、对环境威胁最小的近海区域提供了最大保护，珊瑚海计划也面临同样的指责。

questionGroups.sourceText: 《西游记》(Journey to the West)也许是中国文学四大经典小说中最具影响力的一部，当然也是在国外最广为人知的一部小说。这部小说描绘了著名僧侣玄装在三个随从的陪同下穿越中国西部地区前往印度取经 (Buddhist scripture) 的艰难历程。虽然故事的主题基于佛教，但这部小说采用了大量中国民间故事和神话的素材，创造了各种栩栩如生的人物和动物形象。其中最著名的是孙悟空，他与各种各样妖陇作斗争的故事几乎为每个中国孩子所熟知。

answer.modelTranslation: Journey to the West is perhaps the most influential of the four great classical novels of Chinese literature, and certainly the most widely known abroad. The novel depicts the arduous journey of the renowned monk Xuanzang, accompanied by three followers, as he travels through the western regions of China to India to obtain Buddhist scriptures. Although the theme of the story is based on Buddhism, the novel incorporates a wealth of Chinese folk tales and mythology, creating a variety of vivid characters and animal images. Among them, the most famous is Sun Wukong, whose stories of fighting against various demons are familiar to almost every Chinese child.
translationNotes: 注意'西游记'的英文翻译，应为'Journey to the West'
'穿越中国西部地区'可译为'travels through the western regions of China'
'取经'指'获取佛教经文'，译为'obtain Buddhist scriptures'
'栩栩如生'形容形象生动，可译为'vivid'
'与各种各样妖魔作斗争'可译为'fighting against various demons'
scoringPoints: 准确翻译专有名词'西游记'
恰当表达'最有影响力的'和'广为人知'
准确使用'栩栩如生'的表达
流畅表达'与各种各样妖魔作斗争'
词汇选择准确(influential, widely known等)
